title: מחקר חדש על בונובואים מערער את נרטיב 'הזכר הצייד'

cluster.headline: קופה ראשית: המחקר שעשוי לשנות את ההנחות לגבי האדם הקדום

fetched_notes: Haaretz translation of a NYT piece (by Taylor Mitchell Brown). Headline on Haaretz's homepage frames it as a study 'that may change assumptions about early humans' (האדם הקדום), but the actual study (Current Biology) is about wild BONOBOS (a great ape), not early humans/hominins directly — the human-evolution angle is an inference/extrapolation, not what the study itself measured. Study: two wild bonobo groups, Salonga National Park, DR Congo; observations Feb 2014-Aug 2023 (~9 years); 158 hunting trips recorded, females led 99, males led 59; typically older/dominant females lead; most common prey = red colobus monkey, groups of up to 20 females attacking similar-sized colobus groups; females control meat distribution/alliance-building, sometimes taking meat from males. Lead researchers: Dr. Gottfried Hohmann (Max Planck Institute for Behavior of Animals, lead author) and Dr. Barbara Fruth (same institute, co-author). Outside comment: Dr. Jake Brooker (Utrecht University, not involved) says findings could change how we think about early human hunting roles -- this is explicitly framed as a researcher's speculative extension, not a finding of the study itself.

claims_seed.claim: Haaretz headline framing: this is a study 'about early humans' (אדם קדום), when the actual published research (Current Biology) studied wild bonobos, not human/hominin remains or behavior directly
